Tezacaftor and Moderate CYP3A Inhibitors: When co-administering tezacaftor with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor, closely monitor the patient and adjust the dosage of tezacaftor as necessary to avoid potential adverse effects. 2. Erythromycin Stearate and Thiamine: Erythromycin stearate reduces the levels or efficacy of thiamine by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction is relevant only when both agents are administered orally. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 3. Erythromycin Stearate and Tinidazole: Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 4. Erythromycin Stearate and Tobramycin: Erythromycin stearate elevates the levels or effects of tobramycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 5. Erythromycin Stearate and Tofacitinib: Erythromycin stearate increases tofacitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. While no specific dose adjustment is recommended when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the tofacitinib dose if combined with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. Monitor the patient closely. 6. Erythromycin Stearate and Tolvaptan: Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 7. Erythromycin Stearate and Trabectedin: Erythromycin stearate increases trabectedin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient. 8. Erythromycin Stearate and Tramadol: Erythromycin stearate elevates tramadol levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. This may necessitate a reduced tramadol dose or adjustment of dosing intervals. Be aware of the increased risk of serious adverse events, including seizures and serotonin syndrome. Monitor the patient closely. 9. Erythromycin Stearate and Trazodone: Erythromycin stearate increases trazodone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 10. Erythromycin Stearate and QTc Interval Prolongation: Erythromycin stearate, when combined with drugs such as trimethoprim, triptorelin, tropisetron, valbenazine, or voriconazole, can prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes and other serious arrhythmias. Modify therapy or monitor the patient closely. 11. Erythromycin Stearate and Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where even minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Monitor the patient closely. 12. Erythromycin Stearate and Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec: Co-administration of erythromycin stearate with valoctocogene roxaparvovec may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity, as both agents can elevate liver enzyme levels. Monitor liver function closely and consider alternative medications if potential drug interactions are identified. 13. Erythromycin Stearate and Valsartan: Erythromycin stearate increases valsartan levels by inhibiting the hepatic uptake transporter OATP1B1. This interaction may lead to increased systemic exposure to valsartan. Monitor the patient closely. 14. Erythromycin Stearate and Vardenafil: Erythromycin stearate increases vardenafil levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the vardenafil dose to 5 mg per 24 hours. Monitor the patient closely. 15. Erythromycin Stearate and Vinblastine: Erythromycin stearate increases vinblastine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. 16. Erythromycin Stearate and Vitamin K1 (Phytomenadione): Erythromycin stearate reduces the levels or efficacy of vitamin K1 by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient. 17. Erythromycin Stearate and Voclosporin: Erythromycin stearate increases voclosporin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor the patient closely and modify therapy as needed. 18. Erythromycin Stearate and Zaleplon: Erythromycin stearate increases zaleplon levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 19. Erythromycin Stearate and Zolpidem: Erythromycin stearate increases zolpidem levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. 20. Erythromycin Stearate and Zonisamide: Erythromycin stearate increases zonisamide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient.
